reading.body:
Vantage Santa Clara CA2 publishes 75 MW of IT capacity across 541,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 75 MW supports roughly 1,875 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a conventional enterprise density, the same power supports roughly 7,500 racks. The arithmetic is 75,000 kW divided by the assumed rack draw, and the result is a planning estimate, not an operator claim. The floor area works out to about 285 square feet per rack at the higher density, which is consistent with wide-aisle GPU configurations but cannot be confirmed without a published layout.

No certifications appear in the published specifications for this facility, so none can be read for what workloads they qualify the campus to host.

Among the 103 California facilities this site has mapped, only five publish a megawatt figure, and their combined total is 170 MW. CA2 accounts for 75 of those 170 MW, or 44 percent of all published capacity in the state, and it ranks first by that measure. That share is an artifact of how few operators publish figures, not a claim about California's total data center power, and the remaining 98 mapped facilities carry no published number at all.
